To: Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and Honorable members of the committee From: Audrey Piltch Re: Testimony in Support of LD 108, An Act to Authorize the Release of Military Records to the Office of Chief Medical Examiner for the Purposes of Suicide Reporting and Prevention
I am writing to you as a recent graduate of Freeport High School and a young adult who was born and raised in Maine, urging you to vote "ought to pass" on LD 108.
I was a senior in high school during the Lewiston shootings, when the spontaneous afternoon my friend spent at my house turned into a two-night sleepover as she worried for her family living on the edge of Durham, not knowing if it was safe to return. When we later read the news of Robert Card's history of mental health struggles leading to the shootings and his suicide, it was clear the signs were there. Card joined the Army in 2002, and though he never saw combat, the many others who do struggle for years afterward with PTSD.
By putting this bill into effect, we can prevent the violence and pain that the state felt after the harm Card did to others and himself. Mental health has been recognized as an important part of human well-being somewhat recently in the history of medicine, but it's clear that efforts made towards complete health in the body and mind are increasingly important--especially in an age of loneliness and disconnect facilitated by technology.
With the goal of a greater awareness of mental health struggles and improving support for those fighting self-harm and suicidal thoughts, I encourage you to support LD 108.
Respectfully submitted, Audrey Piltch Freeport

Testimony in Support of:
L.D. 108, "An Act to Authorize the Release of Military Records to the Office of the Chief Medical
Examiner for the Purposes of Suicide Reporting and Prevention" ]oint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and distinguished members of the Ioint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. I'm David Richmond, Director of the Maine Bureau of
Veterans' Services and I'm here today to testify in support L.D. 108, "An Act to Authorize the
Release of Military Records to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner for the Purposes of Suicide Reporting and Prevention" .

In 2023, the U.S. Deparnnent of Veterans Affairs awarded over $4.3 million in cooperative agreements to states and territories to support and provide technical assistance to suicide mortality review committees. These committees are designed to identify and analyze local suicide
deaths, particularly among veterans, to inform and enhance suicide prevention strategies.

Maine was selected as one of 10 states to participate in this groundbreaking effort to understand veteran suicide, identify populations or locations of special concern, and develop data~informed prevention strategies. Without access to these records, the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
may be missing relevant background information that is held by the Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services that may be necessary to identify trends and develop effective prevention measures.
LD 108 would authorize the release of a deceased individual's military records to the Maine Chief
Medical Examiner, in the performance of their official duties and at their request, for the purposes of providing relevant background in the interest of suicide reporting and prevention.
Maine's veteran suicide rate is a grave concern that we are intent on addressing to the best of our ability. LD 108 can help put all relevant available information in the hands of the Medical
Examiner's office, while protecting the veteran's privacy standards, and better position them to
identify trends in veteran suicide that could lead to actions to reduce it.
Thank you for your consideration. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Respectfully Submitted,
David Richmond Director, Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services

Testimony of Representative Morgan Rielly on LD 108, "An Act to Authorize the Release of Military Records to the Office of
Chief Medical Examiner for the Purposes of Suicide Reporting and Prevention"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs

Good morning Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. I am Morgan Rielly, and I represent House District 127, which includes part of Westbrook. I am here today to present LD 108, "An Act to Authorize the Release of Military Records to the Office of Chief Medical Examiner for the Purposes of Suicide Reporting and Prevention."

This bill was brought to me by the Department of Defense, Veterans and Emergency Management (DVEM). DVEM can provide more information during the public hearing regarding Maine's statistics on veteran suicide and their current work on prevention.

LD 108 will allow DVEM to release military records to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner for suicide reporting. By authorizing the sharing of these records, this legislation will help Maine have a clearer understanding of trends in veteran suicide that can aid the state in developing policies for prevention.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration.

District 127: Westbrook
